messages:
Claire (PM): Quick sync — we need to decide sequencing + RICE for the per-route rollout work. Customers keep asking for both Console UI and API hooks. Tradeoff: lower developer friction (API) vs platform completeness / sales enablement (Console). Proposing API-first minimal with Console follow-up. Thoughts?
Dan (Eng): API-first sounds good to me. SDK users can ship faster. Console is higher dev cost (UX + RBAC) and slower.
Tanya (DevEx): Agree on API-first from onboarding POV. We should be explicit about how we score RICE though — 'impact' should map to measurable onboarding metrics (time to first token / first successful rollout).
Michael (Product Ops): Sales/CS pushback: a few enterprise deals require a Console control plane for audits. If we delay Console too long we may lose those deals.
Dan (Eng): What about a hybrid: ship API controls + a read-only Console view that surfaces rollout state and audit logs. That gives sales visibility without full admin UX.
Tanya (DevEx): I sketched a quick RICE calc (very rough):
```
Option A - API-first minimal:
Reach = 300 dev teams in Q1
Impact = 3 (reduced integration time)
Confidence = 70%
Effort = 3 engineer-weeks
Score = (300*3*0.7)/3 = 210

Option B - Console-first full UI:
Reach = 80 enterprise accounts
Impact = 4 (sales enablement)
Confidence = 60%
Effort = 8 engineer-weeks
Score = (80*4*0.6)/8 = 24
```
Tanya (DevEx): Numbers are illustrative but show API-first dominates for velocity and overall ROI.
Claire (PM): Nice. We need to add non-RICE considerations: security/audit bar, compliance for regulated customers, and SLAs for Dedicated. Can we ensure the API path satisfies audit requirements?
Dan (Eng): Yes, API will emit immutable audit events to our audit log and expose them via the same read-only Console. Minimal Console work is mostly plumbing + RBAC display.
Michael (Product Ops): Proposal for launch criteria: 1) API endpoints documented + SDK examples, 2) 2 pilot customers onboarded (one startup, one enterprise), 3) Read-only Console showing rollout state + audit logs, 4) Ops playbook for rollback and fallback to default routing. If those pass, we ship.
Claire (PM): Love it. Also add a quality gate: no regressions in routing fallback tests and latency delta < 5ms for common paths.
Dan (Eng): Implementation plan: week 1-2 API + tests, week 3 onboard pilot, week 4 Console read-only and rollout. Canary planned for small subset.
deploy-bot: :robot_face: Canary rollout scheduled for 1758890400 to prod-canary cluster (50 users).
Michael (Product Ops): I'll escalate to sales and give them the read-only demo so they can close the deals while we build full Console.
Tanya (DevEx): I'll prepare the quickstart and a one-pager showing how to use the API and the Console read-only view — reduces developer friction while we iterate. :rocket:
Claire (PM): Okay—next steps: Dan to own API PR, Tanya to draft quickstart, Michael to coordinate customer pilots. We reconvene Thurs AM to review canary metrics. :thumbsup:
